title: The derivative as a function
competency: Find the derivative function from the definition and use its notations.

keywords.def: f′(a): the gradient of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)).
Having a derivative: the difference quotient settles at one value from both sides.

en.text: Doing the limit at a general x gives a new function f′(x) = what (f(x + h) − f(x))/h approaches as h → 0. It is defined only where that value exists and is the same from both sides. Other names: dy/dx, d/dx f(x), Df(x). Basic results: (k)′ = 0, (x²)′ = 2x, (√x)′ = 1/(2√x), (1/x)′ = −1/x².

am.text: በአጠቃላይ x ላይ ገደቡን ስንሰራ አዲስ ፋንክሽን f′(x) እናገኛለን። ሌሎች ምልክቶች፡ dy/dx, d/dx f(x), Df(x)።

screens.title: One formula for every point
screens.ask: For f(x) = x², the gradient is 4 at x = 2 and −2 at x = −1. Which formula gives the gradient at any x?
screens.after:
Test each formula at both points.
2x: 2(2) = 4 and 2(−1) = −2. Both match.
x² gives 4 and 1, so it fails at x = −1.
The formula 2x is the derivative function f′(x).

screens.title: The derivative as a function
paras: f′(x) is what (f(x + h) − f(x))/h approaches as h → 0.
Its domain is the x-values where f is differentiable.
Another form: f′(x) = (f(t) − f(x))/(t − x) as t gets very close to x.
screens.note: The derivative is the exact rate at which one quantity changes with respect to another.

screens.title: A corner: y = |x|
screens.ask: The dots lie on y = |x|. Tap them and compare the slopes.

points.name: O
points.info: The corner. Left slope −1, right slope +1. No single tangent, so f′(0) does not exist.

screens.title: Notations
paras: If y = f(x), these all mean the derivative:

screens.title: Key word
defs: f′(a): the gradient of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)).

screens.text: Use the definition to find the derivative of x³: (x³)′ =
screens.why:
(x + h)³ = x³ + 3x²h + 3xh² + h³.
Subtract x³: 3x²h + 3xh² + h³.
Divide by h: 3x² + 3xh + h².
As h → 0: 3x².
Trap: 3x³ keeps the old power.

screens.title: Match each notation with how it is read
screens.why:
All four mean the same thing: the derivative of y = f(x).
f′(x) is read "f prime of x".
dy/dx is read "dee y by dee x".
d/dx f(x) is "d by dx of f(x)"; Dₓ f is "D of f".

screens.text: Differentiability of f(x) = |x|: where is f′(x) NOT defined?
screens.why:
For x > 0, |x| = x: gradient 1.
For x < 0, |x| = −x: gradient −1.
At 0 the quotient is |h|/h: 1 if h > 0, −1 if h < 0.
The two sides differ, so f′(0) does not exist.
The graph has a sharp corner at 0.

screens.text: Use the definition to find the derivative of 1/x: (1/x)′ =
screens.why:
1/(x + h) − 1/x = (x − (x + h))/(x(x + h)) = −h/(x(x + h)).
Divide by h: −1/(x(x + h)).
As h → 0: −1/x².
Trap: 1/x² misses the minus sign. 1/x falls as x grows.

screens.text: True or false: if f(x) = 7 for every x, then f′(x) = 0.
screens.why:
f(x + h) − f(x) = 7 − 7 = 0.
Divide by h: 0/h = 0.
A constant never changes, so its rate is 0. True.

From the definition, (√x)′ = 1/(2√x).
The factor 2 multiplies every quotient, so it stays.
2 × 1/(2√x) = 1/√x.
Trap: 1/(2√x) forgets the factor 2.

screens.ask: Work backwards: the tangent to y = 1/x has gradient −1/9 at x = ___ (x > 0)

items.text: Use the definition: for f(x) = x, f′(x) =
items.why:
f(x + h) − f(x) = (x + h) − x = h.
Divide by h: 1.
So f′(x) = 1: the line y = x has slope 1.

items.text: Use the definition: for f(x) = x³, f′(x) =
items.why:
(x + h)³ − x³ = 3x²h + 3xh² + h³.
Divide by h: 3x² + 3xh + h².
As h → 0: 3x².

items.text: Use the definition: for f(x) = 1/x, f′(x) =
items.why:
1/(x + h) − 1/x = −h/(x(x + h)).
Divide by h: −1/(x(x + h)).
As h → 0: −1/x².

items.text: Use the definition: for f(x) = 2√x, f′(x) =
items.why:
2(√(x + h) − √x)/h. Multiply by √(x + h) + √x.
The top becomes 2h. Cancel h: 2/(√(x + h) + √x).
As h → 0: 2/(2√x) = 1/√x.

items.text: Where does the derivative of f(x) = x² exist? f′(x₀) exists for
items.why:
(f(x₀ + h) − f(x₀))/h = 2x₀ + h.
As h → 0 this gives 2x₀ for every x₀.
No point causes trouble: all real x₀.

items.text: Where does the derivative of f(x) = |x| exist? f′(x₀) exists for
items.why:
For x₀ > 0 the gradient is 1. For x₀ < 0 it is −1.
At x₀ = 0 the right side gives 1, the left side −1.
No single value, so f′(0) does not exist.
Answer: all x₀ ≠ 0.

items.text: Where does the derivative of f(x) = 1/x exist? f′(x₀) exists for
items.why:
f is not defined at x = 0, so f′(0) cannot exist.
For x₀ ≠ 0, f′(x₀) = −1/x₀².
Answer: all x₀ ≠ 0.

test.text: Find the derivative of the constant 5: (5)′ =
test.why:
f(x + h) − f(x) = 5 − 5 = 0.
0/h = 0.
The derivative of any constant is 0.

(x + h)² − x² = 2xh + h².
Divide by h: 2x + h.
As h → 0: 2x.

test.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = √x at x = 4: f′(4) = ___
Find the derivative of f(x) = 1/x at x = −2: f′(−2) = ___
test.why:
f′(x) = −1/x².
f′(−2) = −1/(−2)² = −1/4.
Trap: (−2)² = 4 is positive, so the answer stays negative.

test.text: Which function is not differentiable at x = 0?
test.why:
|x| has slope −1 on the left of 0 and 1 on the right.
At 0 the two sides differ: a sharp corner.
x², x³ and 3x + 1 are smooth there: f′(0) = 0, 0 and 3.
